body.statement: For any nonempty subset \(S\subseteq I\) of cardinality \(t\) and any completed midrank vector, \(\sum_{i\in S}r_i(b)\ge t(t+1)/2\). Equality holds if and only if every label in \(S\) is strictly below every label outside \(S\). In particular, if the \(t\) labels in \(S\) all have rank at most \((t+1)/2\), they form the unique lowest tied block and each has rank \((t+1)/2\).
body.justification: The equality characterization is the load-bearing converse that prevents tie faces from creating false graph certificates.
body.gap: Classical midrank identities give the total rank sum, but the subset equality condition is the exact combinatorial lemma required by this reduction.
body.consumer: A machine-checked version closes the remaining proof bottleneck in the NP-hardness argument.
body.proof_tex:
For distinct labels \(i,j\), define
\[
\phi_{ij}=\mathbf 1\{b_j<b_i\}+\frac12\mathbf 1\{b_j=b_i\}.
\]
The midrank definition is equivalently
\[
r_i(b)=1+\sum_{j\ne i}\phi_{ij}.
\]
For each unordered pair \(\{i,j\}\), trichotomy of real numbers gives
\(\phi_{ij}+\phi_{ji}=1\), including the tied case, where both summands equal \(1/2\).

Let \(\varnothing\ne S\subseteq I\) have \(|S|=t\).  Summing first over pairs internal to \(S\) and then over cross-pairs gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
\sum_{i\in S}r_i(b)
&=t+\sum_{\{i,j\}\subseteq S}(\phi_{ij}+\phi_{ji})
  +\sum_{\substack{i\in S\\ j\notin S}}\phi_{ij}\\
&=t+\binom{t}{2}
  +\sum_{\substack{i\in S\\ j\notin S}}\phi_{ij}\\
&\ge \frac{t(t+1)}2.
\end{aligned}
\]
Every cross-term is nonnegative.  Equality holds exactly when every such term is zero.  For real outcomes, \(\phi_{ij}=0\) is equivalent to \(b_i<b_j\).  Hence equality holds if and only if every label in \(S\) is strictly below every label outside \(S\).

Now suppose each \(i\in S\) has \(r_i(b)\le(t+1)/2\).  The displayed lower bound and the coordinatewise upper bounds imply
\[
\frac{t(t+1)}2
\le\sum_{i\in S}r_i(b)
\le\frac{t(t+1)}2.
\]
Both inequalities are equalities.  Thus each \(r_i(b)=(t+1)/2\), and the equality characterization places all of \(S\) strictly below its complement.  Distinct outcome blocks have strictly increasing midranks, so the equal ranks within \(S\) imply that its labels are tied.  Therefore \(S\) is the unique lowest tied block, as claimed.
